updated_issues.title: G9-X2: Gen 9 readers on the reading bench (tricks saved a board beside nats)
updated_issues.body:
G9-X2: Gen 9's readers scored on p41's reading bench, in double-dummy tricks saved a board, with nats beside.

**What is in it**

- `scripts/gen8_reading_bench.py`: p41's bench, a snapshot of `feature/gen8-p41-20261112` (bb1cd2c in 57696ab, updated to cdde42a in c11fbee as p41 asked), unchanged; to be dropped at the base swap.
- `scripts/gen9_reading_bench.py`, around the bench without changing its pools or its report:
  - `pools` on E9-7's held-out tables against one BEN version, at the house bots' decisions only (BEN's own decisions say nothing about how a house bot reads); or on any folder of tables, with `--deciders declarer`.
  - `relabel`: E9-4 part 1's tables with the defenders' spots drawn again by a declared scheme at an honesty, with E9-4's seeds (the swap counts match E9-4's rows).
  - `readings`: the log weight a bot spec gives every stored layout after `meet()` (the table's opponent, or `NAME=BOT@ID`), with its own factors and signal terms, stored as the bench stores a net, so the bench's report scores it at exponent 1. Two readers that are not bot specs: `--head-reading` (E9-14: the opposing declarer read by a per-player head) and `--expert-reading` (E9-15: the opposing defenders' spots read by a signal expert).
  - `box`: one argv for a box job (fetch the feeds, pools in shards, readings), resumable from its saved part files.
  - `report`: the bench's report on the part files every reading has reached.
- `scripts/gen9_reading_bench_report.py`: the nats-and-tricks tables, by trick band and by declarer or defender deciding, standard errors by deal.
- `tests/test_gen9_reading_bench.py`: two BEN tables (pools, Gen 8's and Gen 9's readings, report; Gen 8's reading of partner equals the stored net's, of BEN is 0.3 of it, the emission model changes only the reading of BEN) and one relabelled table.

**Carried with it.** This branch is based on `feature/gen9-signals-v2`, which `feature/gen9` does not have yet: the signal code it scores (SignalPlayer with emission tables, `signal_experience`, `configs/carding/ben16.json` and `ben64.json`, `r9b-32`), E9-14's `play_head` and E9-15's `signal_expert`, and one fix found here: `SignalModel.emitted` now treats a class of one card as certain (8be31d6). Review the bench parts as G9-X2; the rest is the signals branch's work, merged so that the bench can run it.

**Report.** `reports/gen9-reading-bench-2026-11-12` (300 held-out tables a version, house decisions, paired): E9-7's emission model of BEN is worth +0.021 ± 0.023 (BEN 16) and +0.009 ± 0.023 (BEN 64) tricks a board over Gen 8; E9-15's expert adds nothing measurable; E9-14's head on BEN's declarer play +0.013 ± 0.012 and +0.035 ± 0.014. E9-16 part 1b on p41's house pools: `reports/gen9-leakage-classes-2026-11-12` (which equal card we play is worth 0.038 ± 0.013 tricks a board to a reader of our strength). Still to come on this branch: reading (2), the relabelled E9-4 tables (box jobs `g9-x2-rel-std-80`, `-50`), and E9-16 part 1c.

Reviewer: bill (per G9-X2).

updated_issues.title: play/: a web server where people play bridge against Sid
updated_issues.body:
**Problem.** Max wants people to be able to play against Sid. Sid is none of the current bots, and the site should be ready for it: anonymously as South with three Sids, or with a free account, two people North–South against two Sids; a board-by-board score; history kept in the account; no matches.

**What this adds** (`play/`, self-contained; nothing in `bridge_harness/` or `ops/` changes):

- FastAPI server with long-polled tables, SQLite accounts (scrypt), sessions, board history and replays, a vanilla-JS page.
- Bot workers in separate processes that load one **bundle**: a bot spec, its artifacts checked by sha256, and the source commit that runs it. The first recipe is `8s-32` (Gen 8 standard), copied from the `gen8-s7-azure1` cohort manifest at source `792c4cb`. It is marked `stand_in`, and the page says so. Bots plug in through the **Sid contract** (`bid()`, `play()`; see `sidplay/engine.py`). `ArenaSid` is the default adapter for anything the arena runtime builds, so installing Sid means a new recipe and no server changes.
- Each board's IMPs come from comparing against Sid's own table: Sid plays the same deal at all four seats in a background worker.
- Claims are judged double dummy from the current position. A refusal reveals nothing about the hidden hands.
- Deployment through boxctl: `install.sh` (unprivileged `sidplay` user, `/opt/sidplay`, systemd unit at `Nice=-10`, 127.0.0.1 only), `expose.sh` (one NSG rule for 80/443 to the host VM only, plus a DNS label), `caddy.sh` (HTTPS).

**Information boundary.** A browser gets only the hands its seat may see. A bot gets the game's `Observation` for the controlling seat. The full deal reaches a worker only for the claim referee and for Sid's own table.

**Tested**
- 8 tests: 6 API tests against a stand-in bot (`cd play && SIDPLAY_ENGINE=fake python -m pytest tests -q`): full boards, the hidden-hand check on every response, accounts and guest adoption, partner tables, claims, the CSRF header; 2 for the Sid contract with a toy bot.
- Full boards in a headless browser against the **real 8s-32 bundle** built from the model releases (desktop and phone width, solo and partner tables).
- **Deployed on azure1** (Max's choice): https://play-sid.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com. Two `smoke.py` boards there under full collector load took about 40 s each, and Sid's table 12–27 s more. Memory is about 2.7 GB.
- `smoke.py` against the real bundle locally: a Sid decision averages 0.14 s (worst 1.5 s on one table); a whole Sid table about 9 s; a board 20–35 s wall time, mostly the deliberate pause between bot cards.

**Not done / limits**
- Live tables are lost on restart.
- No password reset, undo, alerts or defender claims.
- While people play, the host box's collectors lose about one core, and their wall-clock timings are inflated.

Guide: [`play/README.md`](play/README.md).

updated_issues.title: Gen 9 experience pipeline (G9-D7) and the arrival run's runner (G9-D6)
updated_issues.body:
Gen 9 work in progress (dave, tasks G9-D7 and G9-D6). No collector, feed, `gh-pages` registry or dashboard is touched.

**This branch contains two unmerged branches:** `feature/gen9-bidding-cards` (bill, PR #26, open) and `feature/gen9-signals-v2` (sam, no PR yet). It uses bill's `bidding_delta`, `profile_evidence` and the guests' bidding, and sam's `card_delta`, carding packages and `experience_honesty`. Merge those first, or with this. The commits that are mine are listed below.

**G9-D7: the experience pipeline** (`bridge_harness/arena9_pipeline.py`, `scripts/arena9.py`)
- **Arrival.** A package that declares a card gets `player_model.arrive` with the card's distance to every held system: the G9-B4 matrix where it has the number, otherwise bill's `card_distance` (computed for `house-dds40k`). The model is stored in the registry log and carried in every epoch manifest.
- **After each board,** with all hands known: bidding statistics go to whoever made the calls at each distinct table (bill's `bidding_delta` with the `profile` evidence), and card statistics to whoever played the cards (sam's `card_delta`). This is only for partnerships with something declared. An occasion is the deal family, seats, auction and opponents, so a replayed deal counts once, while the same deal against a floor's bot and against its control counts twice.
- **At each boundary** the snapshot freezes. A Gen 9 bot whose package asks for it (`epoch_models`) is handed every rostered player's model with that snapshot. Rows and manifests name the snapshot, and `replay` plays a board again from its manifest and snapshot and compares traces.

**G9-D6 pieces**
- **Floors.** Comparison pairs play the same deals, written in the rules file.
- **Packages.** `9a-32`, `8p-32`, `guest-a` and `guest-b`; house packages now declare their profile.
- **Rules.** `rules-arrival.json` and `rules-arrival-rehearsal.json`, plus the events plans.
- **Commands.** `arrival` runs the whole run as one resumable process and restores missing nets; `report` writes the page.

**Also**
- **Runner lock.** One runner per control directory, and a board written twice counts once.
- **will's G9-D4 follow-ups:** a clear error for packages without `bundle.sim`; the demo log kept as `demo-run.txt`; snapshots gzipped with mtime 0.

**Rehearsal** (3 epochs of 24 boards, `guest-a` arriving before epoch 2; records on `transfer/gen9-arrival-rehearsal-20261112`)
- Epoch 3's snapshot equals the merge of exactly the envelopes of epochs 1 and 2.

updated_prs.title: G9-X2: Gen 9 readers on the reading bench (tricks saved a board beside nats)
updated_prs.body:
G9-X2: Gen 9's readers scored on p41's reading bench, in double-dummy tricks saved a board, with nats beside.

**What is in it**

- `scripts/gen8_reading_bench.py`: p41's bench, a snapshot of `feature/gen8-p41-20261112` (bb1cd2c in 57696ab, updated to cdde42a in c11fbee as p41 asked), unchanged; to be dropped at the base swap.
- `scripts/gen9_reading_bench.py`, around the bench without changing its pools or its report:
  - `pools` on E9-7's held-out tables against one BEN version, at the house bots' decisions only (BEN's own decisions say nothing about how a house bot reads); or on any folder of tables, with `--deciders declarer`.
  - `relabel`: E9-4 part 1's tables with the defenders' spots drawn again by a declared scheme at an honesty, with E9-4's seeds (the swap counts match E9-4's rows).
  - `readings`: the log weight a bot spec gives every stored layout after `meet()` (the table's opponent, or `NAME=BOT@ID`), with its own factors and signal terms, stored as the bench stores a net, so the bench's report scores it at exponent 1. Two readers that are not bot specs: `--head-reading` (E9-14: the opposing declarer read by a per-player head) and `--expert-reading` (E9-15: the opposing defenders' spots read by a signal expert).
  - `box`: one argv for a box job (fetch the feeds, pools in shards, readings), resumable from its saved part files.
  - `report`: the bench's report on the part files every reading has reached.
- `scripts/gen9_reading_bench_report.py`: the nats-and-tricks tables, by trick band and by declarer or defender deciding, standard errors by deal.
- `tests/test_gen9_reading_bench.py`: two BEN tables (pools, Gen 8's and Gen 9's readings, report; Gen 8's reading of partner equals the stored net's, of BEN is 0.3 of it, the emission model changes only the reading of BEN) and one relabelled table.

**Carried with it.** This branch is based on `feature/gen9-signals-v2`, which `feature/gen9` does not have yet: the signal code it scores (SignalPlayer with emission tables, `signal_experience`, `configs/carding/ben16.json` and `ben64.json`, `r9b-32`), E9-14's `play_head` and E9-15's `signal_expert`, and one fix found here: `SignalModel.emitted` now treats a class of one card as certain (8be31d6). Review the bench parts as G9-X2; the rest is the signals branch's work, merged so that the bench can run it.

**Report.** `reports/gen9-reading-bench-2026-11-12` (300 held-out tables a version, house decisions, paired): E9-7's emission model of BEN is worth +0.021 ± 0.023 (BEN 16) and +0.009 ± 0.023 (BEN 64) tricks a board over Gen 8; E9-15's expert adds nothing measurable; E9-14's head on BEN's declarer play +0.013 ± 0.012 and +0.035 ± 0.014. E9-16 part 1b on p41's house pools: `reports/gen9-leakage-classes-2026-11-12` (which equal card we play is worth 0.038 ± 0.013 tricks a board to a reader of our strength). Still to come on this branch: reading (2), the relabelled E9-4 tables (box jobs `g9-x2-rel-std-80`, `-50`), and E9-16 part 1c.

updated_prs.title: play/: a web server where people play bridge against Sid
updated_prs.body:
**Problem.** Max wants people to be able to play against Sid. Sid is none of the current bots, and the site should be ready for it: anonymously as South with three Sids, or with a free account, two people North–South against two Sids; a board-by-board score; history kept in the account; no matches.

**What this adds** (`play/`, self-contained; nothing in `bridge_harness/` or `ops/` changes):

- FastAPI server with long-polled tables, SQLite accounts (scrypt), sessions, board history and replays, a vanilla-JS page.
- Bot workers in separate processes that load one **bundle**: a bot spec, its artifacts checked by sha256, and the source commit that runs it. The first recipe is `8s-32` (Gen 8 standard), copied from the `gen8-s7-azure1` cohort manifest at source `792c4cb`. It is marked `stand_in`, and the page says so. Bots plug in through the **Sid contract** (`bid()`, `play()`; see `sidplay/engine.py`). `ArenaSid` is the default adapter for anything the arena runtime builds, so installing Sid means a new recipe and no server changes.
- Each board's IMPs come from comparing against Sid's own table: Sid plays the same deal at all four seats in a background worker.
- Claims are judged double dummy from the current position. A refusal reveals nothing about the hidden hands.
- Deployment through boxctl: `install.sh` (unprivileged `sidplay` user, `/opt/sidplay`, systemd unit at `Nice=-10`, 127.0.0.1 only), `expose.sh` (one NSG rule for 80/443 to the host VM only, plus a DNS label), `caddy.sh` (HTTPS).

**Information boundary.** A browser gets only the hands its seat may see. A bot gets the game's `Observation` for the controlling seat. The full deal reaches a worker only for the claim referee and for Sid's own table.

**Tested**
- 8 tests: 6 API tests against a stand-in bot (`cd play && SIDPLAY_ENGINE=fake python -m pytest tests -q`): full boards, the hidden-hand check on every response, accounts and guest adoption, partner tables, claims, the CSRF header; 2 for the Sid contract with a toy bot.
- Full boards in a headless browser against the **real 8s-32 bundle** built from the model releases (desktop and phone width, solo and partner tables).
- **Deployed on azure1** (Max's choice): https://play-sid.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com. Two `smoke.py` boards there under full collector load took about 40 s each, and Sid's table 12–27 s more. Memory is about 2.7 GB.
- `smoke.py` against the real bundle locally: a Sid decision averages 0.14 s (worst 1.5 s on one table); a whole Sid table about 9 s; a board 20–35 s wall time, mostly the deliberate pause between bot cards.

**Not done / limits**
- Live tables are lost on restart.
- No password reset, undo, alerts or defender claims.
- While people play, the host box's collectors lose about one core, and their wall-clock timings are inflated.

Guide: [`play/README.md`](play/README.md).

updated_prs.title: Gen 9 experience pipeline (G9-D7) and the arrival run's runner (G9-D6)
updated_prs.body:
Gen 9 work in progress (dave, tasks G9-D7 and G9-D6). No collector, feed, `gh-pages` registry or dashboard is touched.

**This branch contains two unmerged branches:** `feature/gen9-bidding-cards` (bill, PR #26, open) and `feature/gen9-signals-v2` (sam, no PR yet). It uses bill's `bidding_delta`, `profile_evidence` and the guests' bidding, and sam's `card_delta`, carding packages and `experience_honesty`. Merge those first, or with this. The commits that are mine are listed below.

**G9-D7: the experience pipeline** (`bridge_harness/arena9_pipeline.py`, `scripts/arena9.py`)
- **Arrival.** A package that declares a card gets `player_model.arrive` with the card's distance to every held system: the G9-B4 matrix where it has the number, otherwise bill's `card_distance` (computed for `house-dds40k`). The model is stored in the registry log and carried in every epoch manifest.
- **After each board,** with all hands known: bidding statistics go to whoever made the calls at each distinct table (bill's `bidding_delta` with the `profile` evidence), and card statistics to whoever played the cards (sam's `card_delta`). This is only for partnerships with something declared. An occasion is the deal family, seats, auction and opponents, so a replayed deal counts once, while the same deal against a floor's bot and against its control counts twice.
- **At each boundary** the snapshot freezes. A Gen 9 bot whose package asks for it (`epoch_models`) is handed every rostered player's model with that snapshot. Rows and manifests name the snapshot, and `replay` plays a board again from its manifest and snapshot and compares traces.

**G9-D6 pieces**
- **Floors.** Comparison pairs play the same deals, written in the rules file.
- **Packages.** `9a-32`, `8p-32`, `guest-a` and `guest-b`; house packages now declare their profile.
- **Rules.** `rules-arrival.json` and `rules-arrival-rehearsal.json`, plus the events plans.
- **Commands.** `arrival` runs the whole run as one resumable process and restores missing nets; `report` writes the page.

**Also**
- **Runner lock.** One runner per control directory, and a board written twice counts once.
- **will's G9-D4 follow-ups:** a clear error for packages without `bundle.sim`; the demo log kept as `demo-run.txt`; snapshots gzipped with mtime 0.

- Its learned honesty is 0.694 (truth 0.8).

standing_relevant_prs.body:
The generation cleanup of `docs/generation-cleanup.md`, run because Gen 8 was authorized on 12 November 2026 (Max, 15:32 UTC) and has been collecting since 16:30 UTC. It closes out Gen 7 and brings the deployed Gen 8 source onto main. It changes documentation, indexes and adopted source. It touches no running collector, frozen run, manifest, feed or `gh-pages`.

g7, the arena's operator, read Gen 7's page at 18:58 UTC and its corrections are in. It is Max's to merge. **Merge with a merge commit**, so the adopted commits stay identifiable.

## Adopted source

Main is an ancestor of all of it. Everything merged without a conflict in code; the one conflict was in `reports/README.md`, an index, where both sides' links are kept.

| What | Commit | Branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gen 8 as Azure and Codex run it | `792c4cb`, plus two page-only commits (`99139a8`, `6950784`) | `feature/gen8-prototype-20261112` |

The three Gen 8 commits are what the live feeds' `recovery/environment.json` name.

## Gen 7 closed

- `docs/generations/gen7/README.md`: the bot, what each collector ran, the day's timeline, results, what it handed to Gen 8, what was and was not merged, documents and feeds.
- Results: `scripts/generation_results.py --generation 7` over the 60 registered Gen 7 sources at 19:20 UTC, 22,021 counted boards. Gen 7.1 against 7.0: 5,639 boards, −0.06 (95% interval −0.13 to +0.01). The rule set for moving to 7.1 self-play (1,000 boards and a 95% lead for 7.1) was not met. Report in `reports/gen7-closeout-2026-11-12/`.
- The pre-arena test has its own row: its bot was not the launched `7s-32` (tree trust 0.25 against 0.3). Gen 7.0 against Gen 6 in the arena is 1,593 boards at +0.28; the test is 1,637 boards at +0.25.
- Gen 7's dated notices moved into `docs/generations/gen7/` with `git mv`; links repaired. A pointer stays at `docs/gen7_prototype_2026-11-11.md` because the policy net release notes link there and release folders are not edited.
- The two sets drained at the switch to Gen 8 (`arena-gen7-1-mix2-azure1-feed`, 381 boards, and six `fresh3` BEN lanes, 105) were registered by the operator during the cleanup and are counted.

## Gen 8 current

- `docs/generations/gen8/README.md` (new), `README.md`, `docs/current-system.md`, `docs/generations/README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/repository-map.md`, `docs/branch-inventory.md` (regenerated: 271 branches), `reports/README.md`.
- `docs/backlog.md`: items 2, 3 and 6 closed (dispositions on Gen 7's page); 11, 13 and 14 opened (12 was opened and closed within the cleanup). Item 11 matters before the next net is trained on arena records: Gen 8's tables are not all house against house, and a training reader must bind each table's systems.
- `scripts/generation_results.py`: its actor order brought up to the dashboard's (`8s-32`, `8c-32`, `71s-32` in front); without that it fails on any Gen 7.1 pair. New `--only` and `--skip` pool a subset of the sources.

## Not merged

Each conflicts with main; listed in backlog item 1 with the conflicting files: PR #15 (`fix/gen7-selfplay-capture-codex-20261112`), PR #13 (`fix/gen6-feed-health-20261111`), `ops/gen7-fast-selfplay-cloud-20261111`, `codex/gen7-independent-selfplay-20261112`, `ops/gen71-19bbdce5-20261112`. The Gen 6 runtime branches were not tried. Gen 9 (`feature/gen9` and the branches around it) stays on its branches.

## Tested

- Full suite at the head of this branch, with the native DDS library and TensorFlow: 336 passed, 1 skipped. The same count after the source merges alone.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests:. python -m unittest test_system.CoreTests`: 11 tests, OK.

- `scripts/generation_results.py`: generation 7 run twice over the 60 sources with the same counts (19:20 and 19:23 UTC); generation 6 run once, and the scored rows of Gen 6's closed table come out as published, except that `6-32` against BEN (16) has 26 more boards from sources that kept publishing after that closeout.

- The 19bbdce5 and independent collectors were told on the coordination board at 18:20 UTC that their deployed commits are in this PR and asked to say if they would rather stay out; neither had answered when this was marked ready.

- No collector was run from this branch. Each of the three Gen 8 sources is running in the arena on its own; their union has passed the test suite only. A collector that moves to main should prepare and preflight as for any new source.
- BEN: no server here.
